Former power industry here. If the average person knew just how often and how long wind farms are disconnected from the grid to balance the supply in the grid, they would not be so eager to build more of them. If you have wind farms in your area, take note of how many turbines are turning at any given moment. You'll see many of them stationary and "parked" across the breeze. This is because demand is low and not many turbines need to generate power. The continuous generation plants (coal, gas, nuclear) are supplying the full demand at that point. Often during off-peak demand times, the entire farm may be disconnected to prevent excess power and the need to balance it. They really do spend a lot of time idling because they are not well suited to handling the demands of the grid. Coal, gas and nuclear plants will always be the ones to handle the majority of the load and they too can be disconnected when necessary if demand drops. Wind and solar are always the first to get disconnected.

People have so little grasp of just how interconnected the gird is, especially in downtown areas, where you might have 5000 people living within a city block. it really is something of a balancing act, and given the amount of equipment and tolerances, actually impressive how the grid is for all intents always on.
